newsitem.title: INDIA: BUDGET HIGHLIGHTS -PART A of Fin Minister's speech.
newsitem.headline: BUDGET HIGHLIGHTS -PART A of Fin Minister's speech.

text.p: Following is a summary of PART A of the annual budget for 1997/98 (April-March) presented by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Friday.
SUMMARY OF FINANCE MINISTER'S SPEECH -- PART 'A'

The second Budget presented in Parliament today, by the Union Finance Minister, P.Chidambaram, underlines the government's commitment to growth with macro economic stability and investment in rural infrastructure and human development.
The foundation of the Budget continues to be based on the Common Minimum Programme of the United Front Government.

The total Budget expenditure is estimated at Rs. 232,481 crore which constitutes the largest ever increase in Plan expenditure by Rs.7958 crore. The increase in the Budget support to the Central Plan is reflected in an increase of Rs.1271 crore in outlay for the Ministry of Rural Areas & Employment with Budgetd estimate at Rs.9096 crore for1997-98. The outlay for social services sector has been substantially enhanced from Rs.11785 crore in RE of 1996-97 to Rs,15707 crore in BE 1997-98.

Maintaining price stability of agricultural commodities and strengthening of rural credit and abolition of controls in rice milling and ginning and increasing subsidy on fertilisers and also reorientation of self-employment schemes, the Budget meets the objectives of basic growth and employment and macro-economic stability.
In his speech, the Minister expressed the government's firm resolve on maintaining price stability, particularly in the prices of foodgrains.

To fight the "battle" of poverty at the grassroot level, a number of schemes have been given a boost. Under the basic minimum services plan, Rs.3300 crore has been provided in the next year's Budget as against Rs.2466 crore in the current year.

This includes Rs.330 crore for slum development. The provision for the accelerated irrigation benefit programme has been enhanced by Rs.400 crore, to the level of Rs.1300 crore in 1997-98. Under the Ganga Kalyan Yojana for taking up schemes for ground water and surface water utilisation Rs,200 crore has been provided.

The self-employment schemes are to be refocussed to provide skill based training, entrepreneurship development and subsidy linked bank credit to one million youth to empower them to start viable small business.

The Planning Commission is presently revising the portfolio of poverty alleviation programmes which will be implemented with effect from April 1, 1997. A new scheme called the Kasturba Gandhi Shiksha Yojana will be inaugurated by the Prime Minister to establish special schools for girl children in districts with low female literacy rates. A provision of Rs.250 crore has been made in the 1997-98 Budget.
AGRICULTURE SECTOR

Emphasising the need to double the flow of credit to agriculture and agro-industries in the next five years, the Finance Minister said that the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund III would be launched in 1997-98 with a provision of Rs.2500 crore.

NABARD is being strengthened with an advance additional share capital of Rs.500 crore. Outlining major policy changes in lifting agriculture controls, the Finance Minister announced repeal of the Rice Milling Industries (Regulation) Act 1958 and the Ginning and Pressing Act 1925. The Licensing price control and requestioning under Cold Storage Order 1964 is also being removed.

He also announced the setting up of an international castor oil Futures Exchange. Small scale industries To ensure the availibility of credit to all the segments of the small scale industry sector, out of the funds normally available for this sector, 40% will now be reserved for units with investment in plant and machinery upto Rs.5 lakh, 20% for units with investments between Rs.5 lakh and Rs.25 lakh and remaining 40% for others.
The Minister announced dereservation of 14 items which at present are manufactured in the small scale sector.

These include rice milling, dal milling, poultry feed, vinegar, synthetic syrups, biscuits, icecreams, automobile parts, corrugated paper and boards. The objective is to bring in new investment and technology flows in these sectors.
HOUSING

To provide credit to farmers to build modest houses, the Minister announced a new plan with loans upto Rs.2 lakhs for building houses on freehold plot in rural areas at normal rates of interests, subject to the borrower putting in one-third of the value of the house.
The National Housing Bank is preparing a scheme which will be launched by the Prime Minister. It is expected that 50,000 loans will be sanctioned in the first year.
EMPLOYEES PF AND GRATUITY

The government announced a revamp of employees provident fund and gratuity scheme to ensure better returns and augment savings. The rate of contribution in all industries and establishments has been increased from 8.33% to 10% with effect from March 1, 1997 for both employers and employees.

In scheduled industries, the rate of contribution will be amended to 12%. The requirement of keeping 20% of incremental PF amounts in the Special Deposit Scheme (SDS) will be withdrawn to enable trustees to invest this portion of the funds in other permitted securities.
The government has also extended the benefit of the ceiling of the gratuity amount payable from Rs.1 lakh to Rs.2.5 lakh for all employees under the Payment of Gratuity Act Insurance.

Underlining the critical need for long-term funds for the development of infrastructure, the Minister said that these were available only in the pensions and insurance sectors. He announced changes in the set up of LIC & GIC for greater autonomy, including the power to make non schedule, non consortium investments and to determine the terms and conditions of service of employees and agents.
He also said that UTI would be allowed to expand its retirement benefit plan into a fullfledged pension fund. LIC would also be permitted to enter into joint ventures in the pension business.
The Health Insurance Sector has also been opened up by enabling GIC to float joint ventures and also allow the entry of selected Indian players.

Describing this as a modest opening of one segment of the insurance sector, the Minister reiterated that only a few Indian companies, that is Indian controlled and with majority Indian ownership, will be permitted to enter the health insurance business.
FERA

Acknowledging that the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1973 needs to be modernised, in view of the country's greater trade and investment linkages with the rest of the world, the Minister said that a new Foreign Exchange Management Act would be introduced later in the year.
The scope of the Export Earners Foreign Currency (EEFC) account is being expanded to allow opening of offices abroad and make investments in overseas joint ventures without reference to the RBI.

The Minister also announced that RBI will appoint a group of experts to prepare a road map towards capital account convertibility by prescribing economic parameters and a detailed timetable for achieving the goal.

The Minister also said that a Bill dealing with money laundering was also being prepared. PSU autonomy Referring to the Common Minimum Programme which promised strengthening of identified public sector companies to enable them to become global giants, Shri Chidambaram said that Navratnas had been identified.

The nine well performing companies are IOC, ONGC, BPCL, IPCL. VSNL, BHEL, SAIL and NTPC. A package of measure would soon be announced to achieve this objective. The government also had decided to delegate more monetary powers to boards of profit making enterprises by doubling the limits for capital expenditure that can be incurred without prior government approval.

He said that government would proceed with the disinvestment of three companies as indicated by the disinvestment commission to ensure long-term viability and sustainable levels of employment. OIL & Gas In his speech the Finance Minister expressed concern at the sharp drop in domestic crude oil production.

He said we must reduce our dependence on imported petroleum products. In this context, he announced the highlights of a new exploration policy. He also said that domestic capital goods suppliers would get deemed export status for this sector and refineries would be allowed to import capital goods at concessional duties at par with the fertiliser sector.

Oil Exploration and Industrial Parks will now qualify as infrastructure for various tax incentives. Telecom The issue of assignability of telecom licences has also been resolved and it was proposed to enter into tripartite agreements among the Department of Telecommunications, the licencee and the lenders. The Budget support for highways has been enhanced from Rs.200 crore to Rs.500 crore.

FIIs & NRIs Underlining the significance of Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs), the Minister further expanded the opportunities for investments by FIIs, NRIs and NRI-OCBs. He proposed that the limit of aggregate investment by these categories in a company would now be raised to 30%.
The limit for venture capital funds investment is also being increased from 5% to 20%.
CORPORATE SECTOR
The Minister announced that five recommendations of the draft Companies Bill would be accepted by the government.

These include the principle of buy-back of shares by companies, merging the provisions of Sections 370 & 372 of the Companies Act for intercorporate investment and loans, provision of nomination facilities for holders of securities, ensuring annual statements from companies raising funds from the capital market to disclose end use of such funds and one time commission to stock brokers for capital gains tax exemption to corporatise their businesses.
The Minister said that the draft of both the new Companies Bill and Direct Taxes Bill would be circulated soon.
SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY

The government proposes a series of initiatives to give an impetus to the development of science and technology and human resources in this sector. The Minister announced a two-fold increase in the outlay for the Technology Development Fund from Rs.30 crore to Rs.70 crore. He also announced new scholarships for outstanding scientists. Outlining the importance of the Information Technology industry, the Minister announced a number of measures to increase production volumes and attract direct foreign investments.
The EHTP/EOU/EPZ units in electronic hardware would now be permitted to sell half of the value of their products, during any 12 month period, in the domestic market and export the other half.
FISCAL DISCIPLINE

Announcing a bold and radical change to strengthen fiscal discipline and provide greater autonomy to the RBI in the conduct of monetory policy, the Finance Minister said that the system of ad hoc treasury bills would be phased out by 1997-98.

A ways and means advance scheme is being introduced to accommodate temporary mismatches in government receipts and payments. Therefore, the concept of the Budget deficit, as presently defined, would not be shown as the Gross Fiscal Deficit (GFD).

The extent of RBI support to the Central Government's borrowing programme would be shown as "Monetised Deficit". He also proposed to introduce a capital indexed bond where the repayment of the principal amounts would be indexed to inflation to provide an effefctive hedge against inflation. The Minister announced a new formula for the devolution of resources from the Centre to the States.

Based on the recommendations of the Tenth Finance Commission, it was proposed to form a single, divisible pool of taxes to be shared between the Centre and the States and adopt the proportion of 29%. This would improve the present share of States.
Revised estimates
The revised estimates for 1996-97 are expected to come down to Rs.202,298 crore. There is an increase of Rs.209 crore in Plan expenditure and a saving of Rs.2571 crore in non-plan expenditure.

The overall Gross Tax Revenue estimated at Rs.132,145 crore will be marginally higher by Rs.174 crore. The revenue deficit has come down from the Budget estimate of 2.5% of GDP to 2.3% of GDP. However, there is no change in the fiscal deficit which remains at 5% of GDP. The total expenditure for 1997-98 is estimated at Rs.232,176 crore.

The focus of the Central Plan would be on rural development, employment and poverty alleviation programme and human resource development. Fertiliser subsidy is being enhanced to Rs.5240 crore for indigenous fertiliser, Rs.1950 crore for imported fertiliser and Rs.2000 crore to decontrolled fertiliser.

An amount of Rs.7500 crore has been earmarked for foodgrains and sugar subsidies. The outlay for defence is Rs.35620 crore. A provision of Rs.4205 crore is being made for the Fifth Pay Commission recommendations other than Defence and Railways, for which seperate provision has been made in the Budget.
